summary: Richard Rorty was a philosopher who earned a bachelor's at the University of Chicago and a PhD from Yale. He held posts at Wellesley College, Princeton University (1962–1982), the University of Virginia (1982–1998), and Stanford University (from 1998).

Richard S. Cohen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Walter M. Spink and Luis Oscar Gómez. He serves as Associate Professor of South Asian Religious Literatures at the University of California, San Diego.

Richard Salomon is an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested 1998–2017) and was a foreign visiting researcher at Soka University in 2007.
Richard Schechner studied at Cornell University, the University of Iowa, and Tulane University. Around 1967, he became a University Professor at New York University's Tisch School of the Arts.

Indologist Richard Schmidt completed his doctorate under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner and his habilitation at Halle-Wittenberg. He lectured at Halle (~1898–1907), served as librarian for the DMG, and became an ordinary professor at Münster in 1910.

Richard Shilleto was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology who studied at Repton School, Shrewsbury School, and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1828–1832). He later taught Robert Alexander Neil.

Richard Sorabji is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Charterhouse School, Dragon School, and Pembroke College. He held academic posts at Cornell University (~1962–1970), King's College London (~1970–2000), and Gresham College (~2000–2006).

Linguist Richard Sproat studied at the University of California, San Diego, and MIT. He held positions at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (2003–2009), Oregon Health and Science University (2009–2012), and joined Google in 2012.

Richard Sylvan was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington and Princeton University. He held an appointment at the University of Sydney (~1963–1964) and became a fellow at the Australian National University in 1971.

Richard Taupier earned MS and doctoral degrees at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. Working in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian, and Buddhist studies, he became Associate Director of Research Development at UMass Amherst and a visiting lecturer at Smith College.

Indologist Richard W. Lariviere studied at Iowa and Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. He served as dean at UT Austin, provost at Kansas, president of the University of Oregon (2009–2011), and president of the Field Museum (2012–2020).

Sinologist Richard Wilhelm studied at the University of Tübingen. He served as a visiting professor at Peking University in 1923 and held the chair of Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt starting in 1924, founding it in 1925.

Indologist and philosopher Richard von Garbe earned his doctorate at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and habilitated at Königsberg. He served as extraordinarius at Königsberg (1878–1894) and held a chair at Tübingen from 1895 to 1927.

Richard von Glahn is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, around 1987 and served as a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.
Rigdzin Shikpo was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under teachers Chögyam Trungpa and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Rigzin Lhundup was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, where his posts are attested in 1959 and 1987.

Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who pursued doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.
Rikizan Ishikawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Komazawa University from ~1962 to 1972 and later served as Professor of Buddhist Studies there from ~1989 to 1997.

Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar Ringu Tulku studied at CIHTS, Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, learning under Dilgo Khyentse, the 16th Karmapa, and Tubten Tsondru. He also founded Bodhicharya.

Rinzin Thargyal completed a Magister degree at the University of Oslo in 1985 in Tibetology, studying under supervisor Fredrik Barth and temporary supervisor Arne Martin Klausen. He later taught Palmo Kyi.
